questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Which of the following is false?
options: If $a * b=a^{b}$ for all $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$, then $*$ is commutative in $N$.
questions.solution:
$a*b=a^{b}$ and $b * a=b^{a}$
\therefore \quad a * b \neq b \neq a ; \forall a, b \in N So, addition is commutative in $ N$.
(b) $(a \times b) \times c=a \times(b \times c), \forall a, b, c \in N$.
So, multiplication is associative in $N$.
(c) $a*b=a^{b}$ and $b: a=b^{a}$
\therefore \quad a * b \neq b \neq a ; \forall a, b \in N So, * is commutative in $ N$ is false.
(d) $(a+b)+c=a+(b+c), \forall a, b$ and $c \in N$.
So, addition is associative in $N$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: - The converse of the contrapositive of the conditional $p \rightarrow \sim q$ is
questions.solution:
We have, p \rightarrow \sim q The contrapositive of $p \rightarrow q$ is $\sim q \rightarrow \sim p$ and converse of $p \rightarrow q$ is $q \rightarrow p$.
$\therefore$ Contrapositive of $p \rightarrow \sim q$ is $\sim(\sim q) \rightarrow \sim p \equiv q \rightarrow \sim p$.
Converse of $q \rightarrow \sim p$ is $\sim p \rightarrow q$.

questions.q: On the set $Q$ of all rational numbers the operation * which is both associative and commutative is given by $a * b=$
questions.solution:
If $a * b=b * a$, then the operation is commutative.
If $(a * b) * c=a *(b * c)$, then the operation is associative.
By option (d),
$\begin{aligned}
&a * b=a+b+a b \\
&b * a=b+a+b a=a+b+a b
\end{aligned}$
Here, $a * b=b * a$, so the operation is commutative.
$\begin{aligned}
(a * b) * c &=(a+b+a b) * c \\
&=(a+b+a b)+c+(a+b+a b) c \\
&=a+b+a b+c+a c+b c+a b c \\
&=a+b+c+a b+a c+b c+a b c \\
a *(b * c) &=a *(b+c+b c) \\
&=a+b+c+b c+a(b+c+b c) \\
&=a+b+c+b c+a b+a c+a b c \\
\text{ Here, }(a * b) & * c=a *(b * c) .
\end{aligned}$
So, the operation is associative.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Which of the following is true?
options: The set of all fourth roots of unity is a multiplicative group
The set of all cube roots of unity is an additive group
$(a b)^{-1}=a^{-1} b^{-1}$ for all $a, b$ in any group $G$
If $(a b)^{2}=a^{2} b^{2}$ for all $a, b$ in any group $G$, then the group $G$ is non-abelian
questions.solution:
(a) Set of all fourth roots of unity is $\begin{aligned}&a=\{1,-1, i,-i\} \\
&\text{ Now, }1 \times(-1)=-1 \in G \\
&\quad 1 \times i=i \in G \\
&1 \times(- i)=-i \in G \\
&(-1) \times i=-i \in G \\
&(-1) \times(- i)=i \in G \\
&i \times(- i)=-i^{2}=1 \in G
\end{aligned} So, it is true.
(b) Set$ of $all cube root of unit is H=\left$\{1, w, w^{2}\right\}$ Now, $\quad 1+w=-w^{2} \notin H$
So, it is false.
(c) It is not true, as this is possible only, when $a$ is an abelian group, i.e. $a b=b a$
(d) We have, \begin{aligned}
( a b)^{2} &=a^{2} b^{2} \\
\Rightarrow \quad(a b)(a b) &=(a a)(b b) \\
\Rightarrow \quad(b)(a) &=(a)(b) \Rightarrow b a=a b
\end{aligned} $\Rightarrow a$ is an abelian group.
So, it is false.$

questions.q: The set of all integral multiples of $5$ is a subgroup of
options: The set of all rational numbers under multiplication
The set of all integers under multiplication
The set of all non-zero rational numbers under multiplication
The set of all integers under addition
questions.solution:
Let $H$ consist of the integral multiple of 5 , i.e. H=\{5 x: x \in I\} This $ H$ is the non-empty subset of $I$.
Now, let $a=5 r$ and $b=5 \mathrm{ s}$ any two elements of $H$, where $r$ and $s$ are some integers.
We have, $a+b=5 r+5 s=5(r+8) \in H$.
$(r+s)$ comes out to be the some integer.
$\therefore a \in H, b \in H \Rightarrow(a+b) \in H$
Hence, $H$ is a subgroup of set of all integers under addition.
